title: How Long Do Dehumidifiers Last? Lifespan by Type
h1: How Long Do Dehumidifiers Last? Lifespan by Type — and How to Stretch It
dek: Most dehumidifiers don't die suddenly. They fade, running a little longer each summer. Here's what's normal, what's not and when to replace yours.
description: How long do dehumidifiers last? Most compressor units run 5–10 years. See lifespan by type, what wears them out early and when to repair or replace.
intro: So, **how long do dehumidifiers last?** A typical compressor dehumidifier lasts **5 to 10 years** with normal care, according to widely cited appliance-service and manufacturer guidance. Whole-house ducted systems tend to run longer — around 8 years on average and up to 15 in drier climates — while a budget portable forced to run nonstop in a genuinely wet basement can wear out in as little as three.

Desiccant units age differently. Instead of a compressor that eventually quits, their absorbent material slowly loses capacity, so performance tapers rather than stopping. And across every type, the biggest factor isn't the brand on the front. It's whether the filter gets cleaned and whether the unit is asked to work harder, colder or longer than it was designed for.
Below, we break down lifespan by type, the three habits that shorten it most, the warning signs of a dying unit and how to decide between a repair and a replacement.

sections.heading: The three things that shorten a dehumidifier's life

blocks.text: Dust blocks airflow over the coils, so the fan and compressor work harder to remove the same water. Over a whole humid season, that strain adds up. GE Appliances recommends checking the filter at least every 250 operating hours; our [maintenance guide](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) has a full schedule.

Compressor units lose efficiency as the room cools, and coils start to frost in the low-to-mid 60s. Auto-defrost lets many models keep going down to about 41°F, but repeated freeze-thaw cycles add wear. If your space is cold most of the year, a [desiccant dehumidifier](/best/best-desiccant-dehumidifier/) is the better long-term tool. Our [freezing up guide](/guides/dehumidifier-freezing-up/) explains the fix.

Boxing up a unit with water in the bucket or on the coils invites mold and corrosion. Empty it, run it on fan-only for a few hours to dry the internals, clean the filter and store it upright somewhere dry.

sections.heading: Signs your dehumidifier is wearing out

items: It runs much longer each season to reach the same humidity target.
The bucket fills noticeably slower in conditions where it used to fill fast.
The compressor clicks on and off rapidly or doesn't start at all.
The coils frost even in a warm room.
It makes new grinding, rattling or buzzing noises.
The air coming out isn't slightly warmer than the room air.

blocks.title: Rule out the easy stuff first
blocks.text: A unit that suddenly stops collecting water is often dealing with a dirty filter, a cold room or a misread humidistat. Work through our [not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/) checklist before assuming it's dead.
If your dehumidifier is within that 5–10 year window and simply running longer, start with a thorough cleaning of the filter and coils. That fixes a surprising share of "dying" units.

items: **Under warranty?** Contact the manufacturer before opening anything.
**Cheap part failed** (humidity sensor, float switch, fan motor)? Usually worth repairing.
**Compressor or sealed-system failure on a portable past 8 years?** Parts and labor often approach the price of a new unit — replace it.
**Whole-house or crawl-space unit under 15 years?** A service call is usually worth it, given the higher replacement cost.

blocks.text: When it's time to retire a unit, don't put it out with the trash — it contains refrigerant. Our guide to [how to dispose of a dehumidifier](/guides/how-to-dispose-of-a-dehumidifier/) explains your options.

sections.heading: How to make a dehumidifier last longer

items.label: Size it right
items.text: An undersized unit runs constantly. Use our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) to match pints to your space.

items.label: Use the humidistat
items.text: Set it to 45–50% so it cycles off instead of running nonstop.

items.label: Clean the filter every 2–4 weeks
items.text: More often in dusty basements or laundry rooms.

items.label: Give it breathing room
items.text: Keep at least a foot of clearance around the intake and exhaust.

items.label: Drain continuously where possible
items.text: A hose or pump avoids constant bucket handling and full-tank stops.

items.label: Store it dry
items.text: Empty, air-dry and clean it before putting it away for winter.

blocks.text: Expect a portable compressor dehumidifier to last 5 to 10 years, a whole-house system 8 to 15, and a portable run nonstop in a very wet space closer to 3 to 5. The habits that protect that lifespan are simple: keep the filter clean, keep the unit in its temperature range and dry it out before storage. If yours is fading, clean it before you replace it — and when it's truly done, our [best dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier/) picks cover every size.

faqs.a: Most portable compressor dehumidifiers last 5 to 10 years with regular filter cleaning. Whole-house systems often last 8 to 15 years, while portables run nonstop in very wet spaces may last only 3 to 5.

faqs.q: How long should a dehumidifier last before replacing it?
faqs.a: Plan on replacing a portable unit somewhere between 5 and 10 years, once it can't hold your target humidity after a thorough cleaning or the compressor fails out of warranty.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For inexpensive parts like a humidity sensor, float switch or fan, often yes. For a compressor or refrigerant leak on an older portable, usually not — the repair can approach the cost of a new unit.

faqs.q: Does running a dehumidifier constantly shorten its life?
faqs.a: Yes. Most portable compressors are designed to cycle on and off. Running one nonstop in a very wet space wears it faster. Use the humidistat, size the unit properly and fix the moisture source if you can.

faqs.q: How long do desiccant dehumidifiers last?
faqs.a: They don't have a compressor to fail, but their absorbent material gradually loses capacity. Expect performance to taper over years rather than stop suddenly.

faqs.q: What is the most common reason a dehumidifier stops working?
faqs.a: A clogged filter or a room that's too cold, both of which cause icing and poor water collection. Our [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/) guide walks through the fixes.
